verses.1:1: Now it happened, after Saul had died, that David returned from the slaughter of Amalek and remained in Ziklag two days.
verses.1:2: On the third day, a man appeared coming from the camp of Saul, with his garment torn and his head sprinkled with dust; and when he came to David, he fell on his face and paid homage.
verses.1:3: And David said to him, "Where are you coming from?" And he said to him, "I have fled from the camp of Israel."
verses.1:4: And David said to him, "What is the matter that has happened? Tell me." And he said, "The people have fled from the battle, and many from the people have fallen and died; moreover, both Saul and his son Jonathan have perished."
verses.1:5: And David said to the young man who was reporting to him, "How do you know that Saul is dead, and his son Jonathan?"
verses.1:6: And the young man who was reporting to him said, "By chance I came onto Mount Gilboa, and Saul was leaning on his spear; meanwhile, chariots and horsemen were drawing near to him,
verses.1:7: and turning behind his back and seeing me, he called out. When I had answered him, 'Here I am,'
verses.1:8: he said to me, 'Who are you?' And I said to him, 'I am an Amalekite.'
verses.1:9: And he spoke to me, 'Stand over me and kill me, for anguish holds me, and all my life is still in me.'
verses.1:10: And standing over him, I killed him, for I knew that he could not live after his fall; and I took the diadem that was on his head and the armlet from his arm, and I have brought them here to you, my lord."
verses.1:11: Then David took hold of his garments and tore them, as did all the men who were with him,
verses.1:12: and they lamented and wept and fasted until evening over Saul, and over his son Jonathan, and over the people of the Lord, and over the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.
verses.1:13: And David said to the young man who had reported to him, "Where are you from?" And he answered, "I am the son of a resident alien, an Amalekite."
verses.1:14: And David said to him, "Why were you not afraid to extend your hand to kill the anointed of the Lord?"
verses.1:15: And calling one of his young men, David said, "Approach and fall upon him." And he struck him, and he died.
verses.1:16: And David said to him, "Your blood be on your head, for your mouth has spoken against you, saying, 'I killed the anointed of the Lord.'"
verses.1:17: Then David lamented with a lament of this kind over Saul and over his son Jonathan
verses.1:18: (and he commanded that they should teach the sons of Judah the bow, as it is written in the book of the righteous), and he said, "Take thought, Israel, for those who have died, wounded on your high places.
verses.1:19: The renowned of Israel have been killed upon your mountains; how have the valiant fallen?
verses.1:20: Do not announce it in Gath, nor announce it at the crossroads of Ashkelon, so that the daughters of the Philistines may not rejoice, and the daughters of the uncircumcised may not exult.
verses.1:21: Mountains of Gilboa, may neither dew nor rain come upon you, nor may there be fields of first fruits; for there the shield of the valiant was cast aside, the shield of Saul, as though not anointed with oil.
verses.1:22: From the blood of those killed, from the fat of the valiant, the arrow of Jonathan never turned back, and the sword of Saul did not return empty.
verses.1:23: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and gracious in their life, were not divided in death either: swifter than eagles, stronger than lions.
verses.1:24: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet with luxuries, who provided golden ornaments for your attire.
verses.1:25: How have the valiant fallen in battle? Has Jonathan been killed on your high places?
verses.1:26: I grieve over you, my brother Jonathan, exceedingly gracious and beloved beyond the love of women. Just as a mother loves her only son, so I loved you.
verses.1:27: How have the strong fallen, and the weapons of war perished?"
verses.2:1: Therefore, after these things, David consulted the Lord, saying, "Should I go up into one of the cities of Judah?" And the Lord said to him, "Go up." And David said, "Where should I go up?" And He answered him, "To Hebron."
verses.2:2: So David went up, and his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal of Carmel;
verses.2:3: and David also brought the men who were with him, each one with his household; and they lived in the towns of Hebron.
verses.2:4: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David to reign over the house of Judah. And it was reported to David that the men of Jabesh-gilead had buried Saul.
verses.2:5: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, "May you be blessed by the Lord, since you have shown this mercy to your lord Saul and have buried him.
verses.2:6: And now the Lord will indeed repay you with mercy and truth; and I also will return favor, because you have done this thing.
verses.2:7: Let your hands be strengthened, and be sons of valor; for although your lord Saul is dead, yet the house of Judah has anointed me as king for themselves."
verses.2:8: Now Abner son of Ner, commander of Saul's army, took Ish-bosheth son of Saul and led him around through the camp,
verses.2:9: and appointed him king over Gilead, and over Geshuri, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
verses.2:10: Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and he reigned two years; but the house of Judah alone followed David.
verses.2:11: And the number of the days that David remained, ruling in Hebron over the house of Judah, was seven years and six months.
verses.2:12: And Abner son of Ner and the young men of Ish-bosheth son of Saul went out from the camp to Gibeon.
verses.2:13: Meanwhile Joab son of Zeruiah and the young men of David went out and met them beside the pool of Gibeon. And when they had come together, they sat down opposite one another, these on one side of the pool and those on the other.
verses.2:14: And Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men rise and play before us." And Joab answered, "Let them rise."
verses.2:15: So they rose and crossed over by number: twelve from Benjamin, on the side of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve from the young men of David.
verses.2:16: And each one, seizing the head of his counterpart, drove his sword into the side of his opponent, and they fell together; and the name of that place was called Field of the Strong, in Gibeon.
verses.2:17: And a very fierce battle arose on that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were put to flight by the young men of David.
verses.2:18: Now the three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel; and Asahel was a very swift runner, like one of the roe deer that live in the woods.
verses.2:19: And Asahel pursued Abner, and he did not turn aside to the right or to the left so as to stop pursuing Abner.
verses.2:20: So Abner looked behind his back and said, "Are you Asahel?" And he answered, "I am."
verses.2:21: And Abner said to him, "Go to the right or to the left, and seize one of the young men, and take his spoils for yourself." But Asahel refused to stop pressing him.
verses.2:22: And again Abner spoke to Asahel, "Withdraw, do not follow me, so that I am not forced to pierce you to the ground, and then I will not be able to lift my face to your brother Joab."
verses.2:23: But he scorned to listen and refused to turn aside; so Abner struck him in the groin with the butt end of his spear and pierced him through, and he died in that very place. And all who passed through that place where Asahel had fallen and died came to a halt.
verses.2:24: Now while Joab and Abishai were pursuing the fleeing Abner, the sun went down; and they came as far as the hill of the aqueduct, which is opposite the valley of the wilderness road in Gibeon.
verses.2:25: And the sons of Benjamin gathered together to Abner, and massed together into a single wedge, they stood on the summit of one hill.
verses.2:26: And Abner called out to Joab and said, "Will your blade rage on to utter destruction? Or do you not know that desperation is dangerous? How long before you tell the people to stop pursuing their brothers?"
verses.2:27: And Joab said, "As the Lord lives, if you had spoken, the people would have withdrawn in the morning from pursuing their brother."
verses.2:28: So Joab sounded the trumpet, and the whole army halted, and they did not pursue Israel any further, nor did they enter into combat.
verses.2:29: Now Abner and his men went away through the plains all that night; and they crossed the Jordan, and having traversed all of Beth-horon, they came to the camp.
verses.2:30: Meanwhile Joab returned, having left off from Abner, and gathered all the people; and nineteen men were missing from David's young men, apart from Asahel.
verses.2:31: But the servants of David struck down three hundred and sixty from Benjamin and from the men who were with Abner, who also died.
verses.2:32: And they took up Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb in Bethlehem; and Joab and the men who were with him walked all night, and at the very dawn they arrived in Hebron.
verses.3:1: So there arose a long conflict between the house of Saul and the house of David: David was advancing and ever stronger than himself, while the house of Saul was diminishing daily.
verses.3:2: And sons were born to David in Hebron, and his firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelitess.
verses.3:3: And after him was Chileab, by Abigail the wife of Nabal of Carmel; and the third was Absalom, the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur.
verses.3:4: And the fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith; and the fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital.
verses.3:5: And the sixth as well was Ithream, by Eglah the wife of David. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.3:6: So while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner the son of Ner was ruling the house of Saul.
verses.3:7: Now Saul had had a concubine named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. And Ish-bosheth said to Abner:
verses.3:8: "Why have you gone in to my father's concubine?" And he, exceedingly angry because of the words of Ish-bosheth, said, "Am I a dog's head against Judah today, I who have shown mercy toward the house of Saul your father, and toward his brothers and his relatives, and have not handed you over into the hands of David, and yet you have searched in me for something to fault on account of a woman today?
verses.3:9: May God do these things to Abner, and add these things to him, unless, just as the Lord swore to David, so I do with him,
verses.3:10: that the kingdom may be transferred from the house of Saul, and the throne of David may be raised up over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba."
verses.3:11: And he could not answer him anything, because he feared him.
verses.3:12: So Abner sent messengers to David on his own behalf, saying, "Whose is the land?" and to say, "Make friendship with me, and my hand will be with you, and I will bring all Israel back to you."
verses.3:13: And he said, "Very well; I will make friendship with you, but one thing I ask of you, saying, 'You will not see my face before you bring Michal the daughter of Saul; and thus you will come and see me.'"
verses.3:14: Now David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, saying, "Give back my wife Michal, whom I betrothed to myself for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines."
verses.3:15: So Ish-bosheth sent and took her from her husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
verses.3:16: And her husband kept following her, weeping as far as Bahurim; and Abner said to him, "Go, and return." And he returned.
verses.3:17: Abner also brought word to the elders of Israel, saying, "Both yesterday and the day before yesterday you were seeking David to reign over you.
verses.3:18: Now therefore do it, because the Lord has spoken to David, saying, 'By the hand of My servant David I will save My people Israel from the hand of the Philistines and of all their enemies.'"
verses.3:19: Now Abner also spoke to Benjamin. And he went to speak to David in Hebron about all the things that had pleased Israel and all Benjamin.
verses.3:20: And he came to David in Hebron with twenty men; and David made a feast for Abner and for his men who had come with him.
verses.3:21: And Abner said to David, "I will arise, that I may gather all Israel to you, my lord the king, and enter into a covenant with you, and that you may rule over all, just as your soul desires." So when David had escorted Abner off, and he had gone in peace,
verses.3:22: immediately the servants of David and Joab arrived, having struck down the raiders, with exceedingly great plunder; but Abner was not with David in Hebron, because he had already sent him away, and he had departed in peace.
verses.3:23: And Joab and the whole army that was with him arrived afterward; so it was reported to Joab by those telling him, "Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he sent him away, and he went off in peace."
verses.3:24: Then Joab went in to the king and said, "What have you done? Look, Abner came to you; why did you send him away, and he went away and withdrew?
verses.3:25: Do you not know Abner the son of Ner, that he came to you for this purpose, to deceive you, and to know your going out and your coming in, and to learn everything that you do?"
verses.3:26: So when Joab had gone out from David, he sent messengers after Abner and brought him back from the cistern of Sirah, with David unaware.
verses.3:27: And when Abner had returned to Hebron, Joab drew him aside to the middle of the gate to speak to him, in deceit; and he struck him there in the groin, and he died, in vengeance for the blood of Asahel his brother.
verses.3:28: And when David heard of this, after the deed was already done, he said, "I and my kingdom are clean before the Lord forever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner;
verses.3:29: and may it come upon the head of Joab, and upon all his father's house; and may there not be lacking from the house of Joab one who suffers a discharge of seed, and a leper, and one who holds a spindle, and one who falls by the sword, and one who is in need of bread."
verses.3:30: Therefore Joab and Abishai his brother killed Abner, because he had killed Asahel their brother in Gibeon in battle.
verses.3:31: Then David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, "Tear your garments, and bind yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn before the funeral of Abner." And King David followed the bier.
verses.3:32: And when they had buried Abner in Hebron, King David lifted up his voice and wept over the tomb of Abner; and all the people wept as well.
verses.3:33: And the king, mourning and lamenting Abner, said, "By no means did Abner die as cowards are accustomed to die.
verses.3:34: Your hands were not bound, and your feet were not weighed down with fetters; but just as men are accustomed to fall before the sons of iniquity, so you fell down." And all the people redoubled their weeping over him.
verses.3:35: And when the entire crowd came to take food with David, while the day was still bright, David swore, saying, "May God do these things to me, and add these things, if before the setting of the sun I taste bread or anything else."
verses.3:36: And all the people heard, and all the things that the king did in the sight of all the people pleased them.
verses.3:37: And all the common people and all Israel knew on that day that it had not been brought about by the king that Abner the son of Ner was killed.
verses.3:38: The king also said to his servants, "Do you not know that a prince and a very great man has fallen today in Israel?
verses.3:39: And I am still delicate, and anointed king; yet these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are hard for me. May the Lord repay the one who does evil according to his malice."
verses.4:1: Now Ish-bosheth the son of Saul heard that Abner had fallen in Hebron, and his hands went limp, and all Israel was thrown into turmoil.
verses.4:2: Now the son of Saul had two men who were captains of raiders: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other was Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin; for Beeroth also was reckoned in Benjamin.
verses.4:3: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and they were foreigners there until that time.
verses.4:4: Now Jonathan the son of Saul had a son who was disabled in his feet; for he was five years old when the news concerning Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel. So his nurse picked him up and fled; and as she hurried to flee, he fell and became lame. And he had the name Mephibosheth.
verses.4:5: Therefore the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, came and entered the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while he was sleeping on his couch at midday. And the female doorkeeper of the house, while cleaning wheat, fell asleep.
verses.4:6: And they entered the house secretly, taking ears of wheat; and Rechab and Baanah his brother struck him in the groin and fled.
verses.4:7: Now when they had entered the house, he was sleeping on his bed in the bedroom, and striking him, they killed him; and having taken off his head, they went away by the road of the wilderness all night,
verses.4:8: and they brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David in Hebron, and said to the king, "Here is the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, your enemy, who was seeking your life; and the Lord has given to my lord the king vengeance today on Saul and on his seed."
verses.4:9: But David, answering Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, said to them, "As the Lord lives, who has rescued my life from every distress,
verses.4:10: surely the one who had reported to me and had said, 'Saul is dead,' who thought he was announcing good news, I seized and killed him in Ziklag, to whom it was fitting to give a reward for the message.
verses.4:11: How much more now, when wicked men have killed an innocent man in his own house, upon his own bed, shall I not require his blood from your hand, and remove you from the earth?"
verses.4:12: Therefore David commanded his servants, and they killed them; and cutting off their hands and feet, they hung them over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in the tomb of Abner in Hebron.
verses.5:1: And all the tribes of Israel came to David in Hebron, saying, "Look, we are your bone and your flesh.
verses.5:2: Moreover, even yesterday and the day before, when Saul was king over us, you were leading out and bringing back Israel; and the Lord said to you, 'You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be leader over Israel.'"
verses.5:3: The elders of Israel also came to the king in Hebron, and King David struck a covenant with them in Hebron before the Lord; and they anointed David as king over Israel.
verses.5:4: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for forty years.
verses.5:5: In Hebron he reigned over Judah for seven years and six months; and in Jerusalem he reigned for thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
verses.5:6: And the king and all the men who were with him went to Jerusalem, to the Jebusite, the inhabitant of the land; and it was said to David by them, "You will not enter here unless you remove the blind and the lame saying, 'David will not enter here.'"
verses.5:7: Yet David captured the citadel of Zion; this is the city of David.
verses.5:8: For David had offered a reward on that day to whoever would strike the Jebusite, and reach the pipes of the rooftops, and remove the blind and the lame who hated the soul of David. Therefore it is said in a proverb, "The blind and the lame will not enter into the temple."
verses.5:9: And David dwelt in the citadel, and called it the city of David; and he built all around from Millo and inward.
verses.5:10: And he went forward, advancing and growing greater, and the Lord God of hosts was with him.
verses.5:11: Hiram king of Tyre also sent messengers to David, and cedar timber, and craftsmen of wood, and craftsmen of stone for walls; and they built a house for David.
verses.5:12: And David knew that the Lord had established him as king over Israel, and that He had exalted his kingdom over His people Israel.
verses.5:13: So David took still more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, after he had come from Hebron; and other sons and daughters were also born to David.
verses.5:14: And these are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
verses.5:17: Then the Philistines heard that they had anointed David as king over Israel, and all of them went up to seek David; and when David heard this, he went down to the stronghold.
verses.5:18: Now the Philistines came and spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.5:19: And David consulted the Lord, saying, "Shall I go up to the Philistines? And will You give them into my hand?" And the Lord said to David, "Go up, for I will certainly deliver the Philistines into your hand."
verses.5:20: So David came to Baal-perazim, and struck them there, and said, "The Lord has divided my enemies before me, just as waters are divided." Therefore the name of that place was called Baal-perazim.
verses.5:21: And they left their carved images there, which David and his men carried away.
verses.5:22: And the Philistines went up yet again, and spread out in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.5:23: And David consulted the Lord, "Shall I go up against the Philistines, and will You deliver them into my hands?" He answered, "Do not go up against them, but circle around to their rear, and you will come to them opposite the pear trees.
verses.5:24: And when you hear the sound of one marching in the tops of the pear trees, then you will enter into battle, for then the Lord will go out before your face to strike the camp of the Philistines."
verses.5:25: So David did just as the Lord had commanded him, and struck the Philistines from Geba until you come to Gezer.
verses.6:1: Now David again gathered all the chosen men from Israel, thirty thousand.
verses.6:2: And David arose and went, and all the people who were with him of the men of Judah, to bring the ark of God, over which the name of the Lord of hosts is invoked, who sits upon the cherubim over it.
verses.6:3: And they placed the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab, who was in Gibeah; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were driving the new cart.
verses.6:4: And when they had brought it out of the house of Abinadab, who was in Gibeah, Ahio, guarding the ark of God, was going ahead of the ark.
verses.6:5: Now David and all Israel were celebrating before the Lord with all crafted wooden instruments, and with harps, lyres, tambourines, sistrums, and cymbals.
verses.6:6: But after they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah stretched out his hand to the ark of God and took hold of it, because the oxen were kicking and tilted it.
verses.6:7: And the Lord was angry with indignation against Uzzah, and struck him for his rashness; and he died there beside the ark of God.
verses.6:8: And David was grieved because the Lord had struck Uzzah; and the name of that place has been called Striking of Uzzah until this day.
verses.6:9: And David was afraid of the Lord on that day, saying, "How will the ark of the Lord come in to me?"
verses.6:10: And he was unwilling to turn the ark of the Lord aside to himself into the city of David, but he turned it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
verses.6:11: And the ark of the Lord dwelt in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-edom and all his household.
verses.6:12: And it was reported to King David that the Lord had blessed Obed-edom and all that belonged to him because of the ark of God. So David went and brought the ark of God from the house of Obed-edom into the city of David with joy; and there were with David seven choirs, and a sacrificial calf.
verses.6:13: And when those who were carrying the ark of the Lord had advanced six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a ram;
verses.6:14: and David was dancing with all his strength before the Lord; moreover, David was girded with a linen ephod.
verses.6:15: And David and all the house of Israel were bringing the ark of the covenant of the Lord with jubilation and with the blast of the trumpet.
verses.6:16: And when the ark of the Lord had entered into the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul, looking out through the window, saw King David leaping and dancing before the Lord; and she despised him in her heart.
verses.6:17: And they brought in the ark of the Lord, and placed it in its place in the middle of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord.
verses.6:18: And when he had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts.
verses.6:19: And he distributed to the entire multitude of Israel, both man and woman, to each one, one cake of bread, and one piece of roasted beef, and fine flour fried in oil; and all the people departed, each one to his own house.
verses.6:20: And David returned to bless his household; and Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How glorious the king of Israel was today, uncovering himself before the maidservants of his servants, and he exposed himself as if one of the buffoons were to expose himself!"
verses.6:21: And David said to Michal, "Before the Lord, who chose me rather than your father and rather than all his house, and commanded me to be leader over the people of the Lord in Israel,
verses.6:22: I will both celebrate and become even more lowly than I have been made, and I will be humble in my own eyes; and with the maidservants of whom you spoke, I will appear more glorious."
verses.6:23: Therefore no son was born to Michal the daughter of Saul until the day of her death.
verses.7:1: Now it happened, when the king had settled in his house and the Lord had given him rest on every side from all his enemies,
verses.7:2: that he said to Nathan the prophet, "Do you see that I live in a cedar house, and the ark of God is placed in the midst of skins?"
verses.7:3: And Nathan said to the king, "Everything that is in your heart, go and do it, because the Lord is with you."
verses.7:4: Now it happened in that night, and look, the word of the Lord came to Nathan, saying,
verses.7:5: "Go and speak to My servant David: 'This is what the Lord says: Will you build a house for Me to live in?
verses.7:6: For I have not lived in a house from that day on which I led the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt up to this day, but I was walking about in a tabernacle and in a tent.
verses.7:7: Throughout all the places I passed through with all the sons of Israel, did I ever truly speak to any one of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, "Why have you not built a cedar house for Me?"'
verses.7:8: And now you will say these things to My servant David: 'This is what the Lord of hosts says: I took you from the pastures, following the flocks, so that you would be a leader over My people Israel,
verses.7:9: and I have been with you in all things wherever you have walked, and I have killed all your enemies from before your face; and I have made a great name for you, like the name of the great ones who are on the earth.
verses.7:10: And I will appoint a place for My people Israel, and I will plant them, and they will live beneath it, and they will no longer be disturbed; nor will the sons of iniquity continue to afflict them as before,
verses.7:11: from the day on which I appointed judges over My people Israel. And I will give you rest from all your enemies; and the Lord foretells to you that the Lord will make a house for you.
verses.7:12: And when your days have been completed and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you, who will come forth from your own body, and I will confirm his kingdom.
verses.7:13: He himself will build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
verses.7:14: I will be a father to him, and he himself will be a son to Me. And if he acts iniquitously in anything, I will reprove him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.
verses.7:15: Yet I will not take away My mercy from him, as I took it away from Saul, whom I removed from before My face.
verses.7:16: And your house will be faithful, and your kingdom forever before your face, and your throne will be firm continually.'"
verses.7:17: According to all these words, and according to this entire vision, so Nathan spoke to David.
verses.7:18: Then King David went in and sat before the Lord, and said, "Who am I, Lord God, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
verses.7:19: Yet even this seemed too little in Your sight, Lord God, unless You spoke also about the house of Your servant for the distant future; for this is the law of Adam, Lord God.
verses.7:20: What, then, will David still be able to add to speak to You? For You know Your servant, Lord God.
verses.7:21: Because of Your word, and according to Your heart, You have done all these great things, so as to make it known to Your servant.
verses.7:22: Therefore You are magnified, Lord God, because there is no one like You, nor is there any god besides You, in everything that we have heard with our ears.
verses.7:23: And what nation on earth is like Your people Israel, for whose sake God went to redeem it for Himself as a people, and to set a name for Himself, and to do for them great and terrifying things upon the earth from before the face of Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself out of Egypt, a nation and its god?
verses.7:24: For You have confirmed for Yourself Your people Israel as an everlasting people, and You, Lord God, have become God to them.
verses.7:25: Now therefore, Lord God, uphold forever the word that You have spoken concerning Your servant and concerning his house, and do as You have spoken,
verses.7:26: so that Your name may be magnified forever, and it may be said, 'The Lord of hosts is God over Israel.' And the house of Your servant David will be established before the Lord,
verses.7:27: because You, Lord of hosts, God of Israel, have uncovered the ear of Your servant, saying, 'I will build a house for you.' Therefore Your servant has found his heart to pray this prayer to You.
verses.7:28: Now therefore, Lord God, You are God, and Your words will be true; for You have spoken these good things to Your servant.
verses.7:29: Begin, therefore, and bless the house of Your servant, so that it may be forever before You; for You, Lord God, have spoken, and with Your blessing the house of Your servant will be blessed forever."
verses.8:1: Now it happened after these things that David struck the Philistines and humbled them, and David took the bridle of tribute from the hand of the Philistines.
verses.8:2: And he struck Moab and measured them with a cord, making them level with the ground; and he measured two cords, one to put to death and one to keep alive; and Moab came to serve David under tribute.
verses.8:3: And David struck Hadarezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah, when he set out to rule over the Euphrates River.
verses.8:4: And when David had captured from his side one thousand seven hundred horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers, he hamstrung all the chariot horses, but of them he left a hundred chariots.
verses.8:5: Syria of Damascus also came to bring aid to Hadarezer king of Zobah, and David struck twenty-two thousand men of Syria.
verses.8:6: And David placed a garrison in Syria of Damascus, and Syria came to serve David under tribute; and the Lord preserved David in all things wherever he went.
verses.8:7: And David took the golden arms that the servants of Hadarezer had, and brought them to Jerusalem.
verses.8:8: And from Betah and from Berothai, cities of Hadarezer, King David took a very great amount of bronze.
verses.8:9: Now Tou king of Hamath heard that David had struck all the strength of Hadarezer,
verses.8:10: and Tou sent his son Joram to King David to greet him with congratulations and to give thanks, because he had overcome Hadarezer in battle and struck him; for Hadarezer was an enemy of Tou. And in his hand were vessels of gold, and vessels of silver, and vessels of bronze.
verses.8:11: These also King David consecrated to the Lord, together with the silver and gold that he had consecrated from all the nations that he had subdued,
verses.8:12: from Syria, and Moab, and the sons of Ammon, and the Philistines, and Amalek, and from the spoils of Hadarezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah.
verses.8:13: David also made a name for himself when he returned after Syria had been captured in the Valley of Salt Pits, with eighteen thousand killed;
verses.8:14: and he placed guards in Idumea and stationed a garrison; and all Idumea came to serve David, and the Lord preserved David in all things wherever he went.
verses.8:15: And David reigned over all Israel; and David also administered judgment and justice to all his people.
verses.8:16: Now Joab son of Zeruiah was over the army; and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was keeper of the records;
verses.8:17: and Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were priests; and Seraiah was scribe;
verses.8:18: and Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were priests.
verses.9:1: And David said, "Do you think there is anyone remaining from the house of Saul, so that I may show mercy to him for the sake of Jonathan?"
verses.9:2: Now there was a servant of the house of Saul named Ziba. When the king had called him to himself, he said to him, "Are you Ziba?" And he answered, "I am your servant."
verses.9:3: And the king said, "Does anyone still remain from the house of Saul, so that I may show the mercy of God to him?" And Ziba said to the king, "A son of Jonathan remains, crippled in his feet."
verses.9:4: "Where is he?" he said. And Ziba said to the king, "Look, he is in the house of Machir son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar."
verses.9:5: So King David sent and brought him from the house of Machir son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar.
verses.9:6: Now when Mephibosheth son of Jonathan, son of Saul, had come to David, he fell on his face and paid homage. And David said, "Mephibosheth?" And he answered, "Here I am, your servant."
verses.9:7: And David said to him, "Do not be afraid, for I will surely show mercy to you for the sake of your father Jonathan, and I will restore to you all the fields of your father Saul; and you will eat bread at my table always."
verses.9:8: And paying homage to him, he said, "Who am I, your servant, that you have looked upon a dead dog like me?"
verses.9:9: So the king called Ziba, Saul's attendant, and said to him, "Everything that belonged to Saul and all his house I have given to the son of your master.
verses.9:10: Cultivate the land for him, therefore, you and your sons and your servants, and you will bring in food for the son of your master so that he may be fed; but Mephibosheth, the son of your master, will always eat bread at my table." Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
verses.9:11: And Ziba said to the king, "Just as you have commanded your servant, my lord the king, so your servant will do; and Mephibosheth will eat at my table, like one of the sons of the king."
verses.9:12: Now Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica; and all the family of the house of Ziba served Mephibosheth.
verses.9:13: Furthermore, Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he ate continually from the king's table; and he was lame in both feet.
verses.10:1: Now it happened after these things that the king of the sons of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.
verses.10:2: And David said, "I will show mercy to Hanun the son of Nahash, just as his father showed mercy to me." Therefore David sent to comfort him through his servants over the death of his father. Now when the servants of David had come into the land of the sons of Ammon,
verses.10:3: the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think that for the honor of your father David has sent comforters to you, and has David not sent his servants to you for this purpose, to investigate and spy out the city and overthrow it?"
verses.10:4: Therefore Hanun took the servants of David, and shaved off half of their beards and cut off their garments in the middle as far as the buttocks, and sent them away.
verses.10:5: When this was reported to David, he sent to meet them, for the men were very shamefully humiliated; and David instructed them, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow, and then return."
verses.10:6: Now the sons of Ammon, seeing that they had done an injury to David, sent and hired for wages the Syrians of Rehob and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and from the king of Maacah one thousand men, and from Ishtob twelve thousand men.
verses.10:7: When David heard this, he sent Joab and the entire army of warriors.
verses.10:8: So the sons of Ammon went out and drew up the battle line before the very entrance of the gate, while the Syrians of Zobah and Rehob, and Ishtob and Maacah, were apart in the field.
verses.10:9: Therefore Joab, seeing that battle had been prepared against him both in front and behind, chose from all the chosen men of Israel and arrayed the battle line against the Syrians;
verses.10:10: and the remaining part of the people he handed over to Abishai his brother, who drew up the battle line against the sons of Ammon.
verses.10:11: And Joab said, "If the Syrians prevail against me, you will be a help to me; but if the sons of Ammon prevail against you, I will come to your aid.
verses.10:12: Be a strong man, and let us fight for our people and the city of our God; and the Lord will do what is good in His sight."
verses.10:13: So Joab, and the people who were with him, entered into combat against the Syrians, who immediately fled from before him.
verses.10:14: Now when the sons of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they themselves also fled from before Abishai and entered the city; and Joab returned from the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.
verses.10:15: Therefore the Syrians, seeing that they had fallen before Israel, gathered together.
verses.10:16: And Hadarezer sent and led out the Syrians who were beyond the river, and brought their army; and Shobach, the commander of Hadarezer's army, was their leader.
verses.10:17: When this was reported to David, he gathered all Israel, and crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam; and the Syrians drew up the battle line opposite David and fought against him.
verses.10:18: And the Syrians fled from before Israel, and David killed of the Syrians seven hundred chariots and forty thousand horsemen; and he struck down Shobach, the commander of the army, who immediately died.
verses.10:19: Now when all the kings who were in support of Hadarezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they were terrified, and fifty-eight thousand fled before Israel. And they made peace with Israel and served them; and the Syrians were afraid to give aid to the sons of Ammon any longer.
verses.11:1: Now it happened, at the turn of the year, at the time when kings are accustomed to march out to war, that David sent Joab, and his servants with him, and all Israel, and they devastated the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah; but David remained in Jerusalem.
verses.11:2: While these things were taking place, it happened that David rose from his bed after midday and walked about on the roof of the royal house; and he saw a woman washing herself opposite him on her roof; and the woman was very beautiful.
verses.11:3: Therefore the king sent and inquired who the woman was. And it was reported to him that she was Bathsheba the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite.
verses.11:4: So David, having sent messengers, took her; and when she had come in to him, he slept with her, and immediately she was purified from her uncleanness,
verses.11:5: and she returned to her house, having conceived a child. And she sent and informed David, and said, "I have conceived."
verses.11:6: Now David sent to Joab, saying, "Send Uriah the Hittite to me." And Joab sent Uriah to David.
verses.11:7: And Uriah came to David. And David asked how well Joab and the people were doing, and how the war was being conducted.
verses.11:8: And David said to Uriah, "Go to your house and wash your feet." And Uriah went out from the king's house, and a royal meal followed him.
verses.11:9: But Uriah slept before the gate of the royal house with the other servants of his lord, and did not go down to his house.
verses.11:10: And it was reported to David by those who said, "Uriah did not go to his house." And David said to Uriah, "Have you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?"
verses.11:11: And Uriah said to David, "The ark of God and Israel and Judah dwell in tents, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord remain on the face of the earth; and shall I enter my house to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? By your welfare and by the welfare of your soul, I will not do this thing."
verses.11:12: Therefore David said to Uriah, "Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will send you away." Uriah stayed in Jerusalem on that day and the next;
verses.11:13: and David summoned him to eat before him and drink, and made him drunk; and going out in the evening, he slept on his bed with the servants of his lord, and did not go down to his house.
verses.11:14: So morning came, and David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah,
verses.11:15: writing in the letter, "Place Uriah at the front of the war, where the battle is fiercest, and abandon him, so that he may be struck down and perish."
verses.11:16: Therefore, while Joab was besieging the city, he placed Uriah in the place where he knew the strongest men were.
verses.11:17: And the men went out from the city and fought against Joab, and some of the people of David's servants fell, and Uriah the Hittite also died.
verses.11:18: Therefore Joab sent and reported to David all the matters of the battle;
verses.11:19: and he instructed the messenger, saying, "When you have finished all the accounts of the war to the king,
verses.11:20: if you see him become indignant, and he says, 'Why did you approach the wall to fight? Did you not know that many missiles are hurled from above off the wall?
verses.11:21: Who struck down Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal? Did not a woman cast a fragment of a millstone on him from the wall and kill him in Thebez? Why did you come near the wall?' you will say, 'Your servant Uriah the Hittite has also fallen.'"
verses.11:22: So the messenger departed, and came and told David everything that Joab had instructed him.
verses.11:23: And the messenger said to David, "The men prevailed against us and came out to us into the field, but having made an assault, we pursued them as far as the gate of the city.
verses.11:24: And the archers directed missiles at your servants from the wall above, and some of the king's servants died; moreover, your servant Uriah the Hittite is dead."
verses.11:25: And David said to the messenger, "You will say these things to Joab: 'Do not let this matter break you, for the outcome of war is varied; the sword consumes now this one and now that one. Strengthen your warriors against the city so that you may destroy it, and encourage them.'"
verses.11:26: Now the wife of Uriah heard that Uriah her husband had died, and she mourned for him.
verses.11:27: Now when the mourning had passed, David sent and brought her into his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. And this thing that David had done was displeasing before the Lord.
verses.12:1: Therefore the Lord sent Nathan to David; and when he had come to him, he said to him, "Two men were in one city, one rich and the other poor.
verses.12:2: The rich man had very many sheep and cattle.
verses.12:3: But the poor man had nothing at all except one little sheep which he had bought and nourished, and which had grown up with him together with his sons, eating from his bread and drinking from his cup and sleeping in his bosom; and it was to him like a daughter.
verses.12:4: Now when a certain traveler had come to the rich man, refraining from taking from his own sheep and from his cattle to provide a feast for that traveler who had come to him, he took the sheep of the poor man and prepared food for the man who had come to him."
verses.12:5: Then David became exceedingly angry with indignation against that man, and he said to Nathan, "As the Lord lives, surely the man who did this is a son of death.
verses.12:6: He shall repay the sheep fourfold, because he did this thing and showed no pity."
verses.12:7: Then Nathan said to David, "You are that man. This is what the Lord God of Israel says: 'I anointed you as king over Israel, and I rescued you from the hand of Saul,
verses.12:8: and I gave you the house of your master and the wives of your master in your bosom, and I gave you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if these things are small, I will add much greater things to you.
verses.12:9: Why then have you despised the word of the Lord, to do evil in My sight? You struck down Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and took his wife to be your wife, and killed him with the sword of the sons of Ammon.
verses.12:10: For this reason the sword will not depart from your house forever, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite so that she might be your wife.'
verses.12:11: Therefore, this is what the Lord says: 'Look, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he will sleep with your wives before the eyes of this sun.
verses.12:12: For you acted in secret, but I will do this thing in the sight of all Israel and in the sight of the sun.'"
verses.12:13: And David said to Nathan, "I have sinned against the Lord." And Nathan said to David, "The Lord also has removed your sin; you will not die.
verses.12:14: Nevertheless, because you have caused the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme on account of this thing, the son who has been born to you will surely die."
verses.12:15: Then Nathan returned to his house. And the Lord struck the little child whom the wife of Uriah had borne to David, and he was despaired of.
verses.12:16: And David pleaded with the Lord for the little child; and David fasted with a fast, and going inside by himself, he lay upon the ground.
verses.12:17: Then the elders of his house came, urging him to get up from the ground; yet he was unwilling, nor did he eat food with them.
verses.12:18: Now it happened on the seventh day that the infant died. And David's servants were afraid to report to him that the little child was dead, for they said, "Look, while the little child was still alive, we spoke to him, and he did not listen to our voice; how much more, if we say, 'The boy is dead,' will he afflict himself?"
verses.12:19: Therefore when David saw his servants whispering, he understood that the little infant was dead; and he said to his servants, "Is the boy dead?" And they answered him, "He is dead."
verses.12:20: Then David rose from the ground, and washed and anointed himself; and when he had changed his clothing, he entered the house of the Lord and worshiped; and he came into his own house and asked that they set bread before him, and he ate.
verses.12:21: Then his servants said to him, "What is this thing that you have done? On account of the infant, while he was still alive, you fasted and were weeping; but when the boy died, you rose and ate bread."
verses.12:22: And he said, "On account of the infant, while he was still alive, I fasted and wept; for I was saying, 'Who knows whether perhaps the Lord may grant him to me, and the infant may live?'
verses.12:23: But now that he is dead, why should I fast? Will I be able to call him back any longer? Rather, I will go to him, whereas he will not return to me."
verses.12:24: And David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her and slept with her; and she bore a son, and called his name Solomon; and the Lord loved him.
verses.12:25: And He sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and called his name Beloved of the Lord, because the Lord loved him.
verses.12:26: Now Joab was fighting against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and was storming the royal city.
verses.12:27: And Joab sent messengers to David, saying, "I have fought against Rabbah, and the City of Waters is about to be captured.
verses.12:28: Now therefore, gather the remaining part of the people, and besiege the city, and capture it, so that when the city has been laid waste by me, the victory may not be attributed to my name."
verses.12:29: So David gathered all the people and set out against Rabbah; and when he had fought, he captured it.
verses.12:30: And he took the crown of their king from his head, weighing a talent of gold, having most precious gems; and it was placed upon the head of David. Moreover, he also carried away very much plunder from the city.
verses.12:31: Bringing out its people as well, he sawed them, and drove iron-shod carts over them, and cut them apart with knives, and passed them through in the mold of bricks; thus he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David and all the army returned to Jerusalem.
verses.13:1: Now it happened after these things that Amnon the son of David fell deeply in love with a very beautiful sister of Absalom the son of David, named Tamar,
verses.13:2: and pined desperately for her, so much so that he became sick because of his love for her; for since she was a virgin, it seemed difficult to him to act dishonorably in any way with her.
verses.13:3: Now Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother, a very shrewd man.
verses.13:4: And he said to him, "Why are you so wasted with leanness, son of the king, day by day? Why do you not tell me?" And Amnon said to him, "I love Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom."
verses.13:5: Jonadab answered him, "Lie down on your bed and pretend illness; and when your father comes to visit you, say to him, 'Please let Tamar my sister come, so that she may give me food and prepare a savory dish, that I may eat from her hand.'"
verses.13:6: So Amnon lay down and began to act as if he were sick; and when the king had come to visit him, Amnon said to the king, "I beg you, let Tamar my sister come, so that she may make two little broths before my eyes, and I may take food from her hand."
verses.13:7: Therefore David sent home to Tamar, saying, "Come to the house of Amnon your brother, and make a savory dish for him."
verses.13:8: And Tamar came to the house of Amnon her brother, and he was lying down. And taking flour, she mixed it, and making it liquid, she cooked the little broths before his eyes.
verses.13:9: And taking what she had cooked, she poured it out and set it before him, yet he refused to eat. And Amnon said, "Put everyone out from me." And when they had put everyone out,
verses.13:10: Amnon said to Tamar, "Bring the food into the inner chamber, so that I may eat from your hand." So Tamar took the little broths that she had made and brought them to Amnon her brother into the inner chamber.
verses.13:11: And when she had offered the food to him, he seized her and said, "Come, lie with me, my sister."
verses.13:12: And she answered him, "No, my brother, do not force me, for this is not lawful in Israel; do not commit this folly.
verses.13:13: For I will not be able to bear my disgrace, and you will be like one of the fools in Israel. Rather, speak to the king, and he will not deny me to you."
verses.13:14: But he refused to yield to her pleas, and prevailing in strength, he forced her and lay with her.
verses.13:15: Then Amnon hated her with a very great hatred, so that the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her before. And Amnon said to her, "Get up and go."
verses.13:16: And she answered him, "This evil that you are now doing against me, driving me out, is greater than what you did before." Yet he refused to listen to her;
verses.13:17: instead, having called the young man who attended him, he said, "Put this woman outside away from me, and shut the door behind her."
verses.13:18: Now she was clothed in an ankle-length tunic, for the virgin daughters of the king used to wear garments of this kind. So his attendant put her outside, and shut the doors behind her.
verses.13:19: And sprinkling ashes upon her head, with her ankle-length tunic torn and her hands placed upon her head, she went walking along and crying out.
verses.13:20: Then Absalom her brother said to her, "Has Amnon your brother lain with you? But now, sister, keep silent; he is your brother; do not afflict your heart over this matter." So Tamar remained, wasting away, in the house of Absalom her brother.
verses.13:21: Now when King David heard these words, he was greatly grieved; yet he was unwilling to grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, since he was his firstborn.
verses.13:22: Moreover, Absalom spoke neither evil nor good to Amnon, for Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated Tamar his sister.
verses.13:23: Now it happened after a period of two years that Absalom's sheep were being sheared in Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim; and Absalom invited all the sons of the king,
verses.13:24: and came to the king and said to him, "Look, the sheep of your servant are being sheared; please let the king come with his servants to his servant."
verses.13:25: And the king said to Absalom, "No, my son, do not ask that we all come and burden you." And although he pressed him, he was unwilling to go, yet he blessed him.
verses.13:26: And Absalom said, "If you do not wish to come, I beg you, let at least Amnon my brother come with us." And the king said to him, "It is not necessary that he go with you."
verses.13:27: So Absalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the sons of the king go with him. And Absalom had prepared a feast like the feast of a king.
verses.13:28: Now Absalom had commanded his young men, saying, "Watch when Amnon is drunk with wine and I say to you, 'Strike him and kill him.' Do not be afraid, for it is I who command you; be strong and be valiant men."
verses.13:29: So Absalom's young men did against Amnon just as Absalom had commanded them. And rising up, all the sons of the king each mounted his mule and fled.
verses.13:30: And while they were still going on the way, a report reached David, saying, "Absalom has struck down all the sons of the king, and not even one of them has remained."
verses.13:31: So the king rose up, and tore his garments, and fell upon the ground; and all his servants who stood by him tore their garments.
verses.13:32: Then Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David's brother, answered and said, "Let not my lord the king suppose that all the young men, the sons of the king, have been killed; Amnon alone is dead, for he was placed in the mouth of Absalom from the day on which he forced Tamar his sister.
verses.13:33: Now therefore, let not my lord the king lay this word upon his heart, saying, 'All the sons of the king have been killed,' for Amnon alone is dead."
verses.13:34: Meanwhile Absalom fled. And the young watchman lifted up his eyes and gazed, and look, many people were coming along a byway from the side of the mountain.
verses.13:35: Then Jonadab said to the king, "Look, the sons of the king are here; according to the word of your servant, so it has happened."
verses.13:36: And when he had finished speaking, the sons of the king also appeared; and entering, they lifted up their voice and wept; and the king also, and all his servants, wept with a very great weeping.
verses.13:37: Now Absalom, fleeing, went away to Talmai, the son of Ammihud, king of Geshur. So David mourned for his son every day.
verses.13:38: And Absalom, after he had fled and had come to Geshur, was there for three years.
verses.13:39: And King David ceased to pursue Absalom, because he had been comforted over the death of Amnon.
verses.14:1: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah, perceiving that the king's heart was turned toward Absalom,
verses.14:2: sent to Tekoa and brought a wise woman from there, and said to her, "Pretend to be mourning, and put on a mourning garment, and do not anoint yourself with oil, so that you may be like a woman already mourning a dead person for a very long time;
verses.14:3: and you will go in to the king and speak words of this kind to him." And Joab put the words in her mouth.
verses.14:4: Therefore, when the Tekoite woman had gone in to the king, she fell to the ground before him and bowed in homage, and said, "Save me, king."
verses.14:5: And the king said to her, "What matter do you have?" She answered, "Alas, I am a widowed woman, for my husband has died.
verses.14:6: And your maidservant had two sons, who quarreled against each other in the field, and there was no one who could restrain them; and the one struck the other and killed him.
verses.14:7: And look, the entire clan, rising up against your maidservant, says, 'Hand over the one who struck his brother, so that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and destroy the heir.' And they are seeking to extinguish my spark that remains, so that neither name nor remnant may survive for my husband upon the earth."
verses.14:8: And the king said to the woman, "Go to your house, and I will give an order on your behalf."
verses.14:9: And the Tekoite woman said to the king, "Upon me, my lord the king, let the iniquity be, and upon my father's house; but let the king and his throne be innocent."
verses.14:10: And the king said, "Whoever speaks against you, bring him to me, and he will not touch you again."
verses.14:11: And she said, "Let the king remember the Lord his God, so that the kinsmen of blood may not multiply to take vengeance, and by no means kill my son." And he said, "As the Lord lives, not one of the hairs of your son will fall to the ground."
verses.14:12: Therefore the woman said, "Let your maidservant speak a word to my lord the king." And he said, "Speak."
verses.14:13: And the woman said, "Why have you devised a thing of this kind against the people of God, and why has the king spoken this word so that he sins and does not bring back his banished one?
verses.14:14: We all die, and like waters that do not return we flow away into the earth; nor does God wish a soul to perish, but He reconsiders, taking thought so that the one who has been cast out may not completely perish.
verses.14:15: Now therefore I have come to speak this word to my lord the king in the presence of the people. And your maidservant said, 'I will speak to the king, if somehow the king may carry out the word of his maidservant.'
verses.14:16: And the king listened, so as to deliver his maidservant from the hand of all who wanted to destroy me and my son together from the inheritance of God.
verses.14:17: Let your maidservant therefore say, may the word of my lord the king be like a sacrifice. For like an angel of God, so is my lord the king, so that he is moved neither by blessing nor by curse; for this reason the Lord your God is also with you."
verses.14:18: And answering, the king said to the woman, "Do not hide from me the thing that I am asking you." And the woman said to him, "Speak, my lord the king."
verses.14:19: And the king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all these things?" The woman answered and said, "By the welfare of your soul, my lord the king, it is neither to the left nor to the right of all these things that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab, he himself commanded me, and he himself put all these words into the mouth of your maidservant.
verses.14:20: In order that I might change the form of this speech, your servant Joab commanded this; but you, my lord the king, are wise, just as an angel of God has wisdom, so that you understand everything on the earth."
verses.14:21: And the king said to Joab, "Look, being appeased, I have carried out your word; go therefore, and call back the young man Absalom."
verses.14:22: And falling on his face to the ground, Joab bowed in homage and blessed the king; and Joab said, "Today your servant has understood that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, for you have carried out the word of your servant."
verses.14:23: Therefore Joab arose and went away to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.
verses.14:24: But the king said, "Let him return to his own house, and let him not see my face." So Absalom returned to his own house, and he did not see the king's face.
verses.14:25: Moreover, there was no man in all Israel handsome and exceedingly graceful like Absalom; from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was not any blemish in him.
verses.14:26: And when he cut his hair (for it was cut once a year, because his thick hair weighed him down), he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the public weight.
verses.14:27: Now three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter named Tamar, of elegant form.
verses.14:28: And Absalom remained in Jerusalem for two years, and he did not see the king's face.
verses.14:29: Therefore he sent for Joab, so that he might send him to the king, but he refused to come to him. And when he had sent a second time, and he had refused to come to him,
verses.14:30: he said to his servants, "You know Joab's field next to my field, which has a harvest of barley; go therefore and set it on fire." So Absalom's servants set the crop on fire. And Joab's servants, coming with their clothes torn, said, "Absalom's servants have set part of the field on fire."
verses.14:31: And Joab arose and came to Absalom at his house, and said, "Why have your servants set my crop on fire?"
verses.14:32: And Absalom answered Joab, "I sent to you pleading that you would come to me, so that I might send you to the king and you might say to him, 'Why have I come from Geshur? It was better for me to be there.' Therefore I plead that I may see the king's face; and if he remembers my iniquity, let him kill me."
verses.14:33: So Joab went in to the king and reported everything to him; and Absalom was summoned, and he entered before the king and bowed in homage upon the face of the ground before him; and the king kissed Absalom.
verses.15:1: Now after these things, Absalom made for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to go before him.
verses.15:2: And Absalom, rising early in the morning, would stand beside the entrance of the gate; and every man who had a case to come to the king's judgment, Absalom would call to himself and say, "From which city are you?" And answering, he would say, "I, your servant, am from one of the tribes of Israel."
verses.15:3: And Absalom would answer him, "Your words seem good and just to me, but there is no one appointed by the king to hear you." And Absalom would say,
verses.15:4: "Who will appoint me judge over the land, so that all who have a case may come to me, and I may judge justly?"
verses.15:5: Moreover, when a man approached him to greet him, he would stretch out his hand, and taking hold of him, would kiss him.
verses.15:6: And he would do this to all Israel coming to judgment to be heard by the king, and he enticed the hearts of the men of Israel.
verses.15:7: Now after forty years, Absalom said to King David, "Let me go and pay my vows that I vowed to the Lord in Hebron.
verses.15:8: For your servant solemnly vowed while he was in Geshur of Syria, saying, 'If the Lord brings me back to Jerusalem, I will sacrifice to the Lord.'"
verses.15:9: And King David said to him, "Go in peace." And he arose and went away to Hebron.
verses.15:10: Now Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the blast of the trumpet, say, 'Absalom has become king in Hebron.'"
verses.15:11: Moreover, two hundred invited men from Jerusalem went with Absalom, going with an innocent heart and completely ignorant of the matter.
verses.15:12: Absalom also summoned Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city Giloh. And while he was offering sacrifices, a strong conspiracy was formed, and the people flocking together increased with Absalom.
verses.15:13: Then a messenger came to David, saying, "All Israel is following Absalom with its whole heart."
verses.15:14: And David said to his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Arise, let us flee, for there will be no escape for us from before Absalom; hurry to leave, or else he may come and overtake us, and bring ruin upon us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword."
verses.15:15: And the king's servants said to him, "Everything that our lord the king commands, we, your servants, will gladly carry out."
verses.15:16: Therefore the king and his entire household went out on foot; and the king left behind ten women who were concubines to guard the house.
verses.15:17: And the king and all Israel, having gone out on foot, stood at a distance from the house;
verses.15:18: and all his servants were walking beside him; and the legions of the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, mighty warriors, six hundred men who had followed him on foot from Gath, were going before the king.
verses.15:19: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why are you coming with us? Return and dwell with the king, because you are a foreigner and have departed from your own place.
verses.15:20: Yesterday you came, and today will you be compelled to go out with us? As for me, I will go where I am going; return, and take your brothers back with you, and the Lord will show mercy and truth toward you, because you have shown grace and faithfulness."
verses.15:21: And Ittai answered the king, saying, "As the Lord lives, and as my lord the king lives, in whatever place you may be, my lord the king, whether in death or in life, there your servant will be."
verses.15:22: And David said to Ittai, "Come, and pass over." And Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all the men who were with him, and the rest of the multitude.
verses.15:23: And everyone was weeping with a loud voice, and all the people were passing over; the king also was crossing the brook Kidron, and all the people were walking toward the road that faces the wilderness.
verses.15:24: Now Zadok the priest also came, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God; and they set down the ark of God. And Abiathar went up until the full number of all the people who had gone out of the city was complete.
verses.15:25: And the king said to Zadok, "Carry the ark of God back into the city; if I find favor in the eyes of the Lord, He will bring me back and show me it and His tabernacle.
verses.15:26: But if He says to me, 'You do not please Me,' here I am; let Him do what is good before Himself."
verses.15:27: And the king said to Zadok the priest, "Seer, return to the city in peace, and let Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, your two sons, be with you.
verses.15:28: Look, I will hide myself in the plains of the wilderness, until word comes from you informing me."
verses.15:29: Therefore Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they remained there.
verses.15:30: Moreover, David was going up the ascent of the Olives, climbing and weeping, walking barefoot and with his head covered; and all the people who were with him also went up with their heads covered, lamenting.
verses.15:31: Now it was reported to David that Ahithophel was also in the conspiracy with Absalom; and David said, "Make foolish, I pray, Lord, the counsel of Ahithophel."
verses.15:32: And as David was ascending the summit of the mountain where he was going to worship the Lord, look, Hushai the Archite met him with his garment torn and his head full of earth.
verses.15:33: And David said to him, "If you come with me, you will be a burden to me;
verses.15:34: but if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I am your servant, king; just as I was your father's servant, so I will be your servant,' you will thwart the counsel of Ahithophel.
verses.15:35: Moreover, you have with you Zadok and Abiathar the priests; and every word that you hear from the king's house, you will report to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.15:36: And their two sons are with them, Ahimaaz the son of Zadok and Jonathan the son of Abiathar; and through them you will send to me every word that you hear."
verses.15:37: So as Hushai, David's friend, was entering the city, Absalom also entered Jerusalem.
verses.16:1: And when David had passed a little beyond the summit of the mountain, Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, appeared to meet him with two donkeys that were loaded with two hundred loaves of bread, one hundred bundles of raisins, one hundred cakes of dried figs, and a skin of wine.
verses.16:2: And the king said to Ziba, "What do these mean?" And Ziba answered, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on, the loaves of bread and the fig cakes are for your servants to eat, and the wine is so that anyone who grows faint in the wilderness may drink."
verses.16:3: And the king said, "Where is the son of your master?" And Ziba answered the king, "He has remained in Jerusalem, saying, 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my father.'"
verses.16:4: And the king said to Ziba, "Let all that belonged to Mephibosheth be yours." And Ziba said, "I beg that I may find favor before you, my lord the king."
verses.16:5: So King David came as far as Bahurim, and now a man from the clan of the house of Saul was coming out from there, named Shimei, the son of Gera; he kept moving forward as he came out and kept cursing,
verses.16:6: and he kept throwing stones at David and at all the servants of King David, while all the people and all the warriors were marching on the right and on the left side of the king.
verses.16:7: Now Shimei was speaking in this way as he cursed the king: "Get out, get out, man of bloodshed and man of Belial!
verses.16:8: The Lord has returned upon you all the blood of the house of Saul, because you seized the kingdom in his place, and the Lord has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son; and look, your own evils are pressing upon you, because you are a man of bloodshed."
verses.16:9: Then Abishai, the son of Zeruiah, said to the king, "Why is this dead dog cursing my lord the king? I will go and cut off his head."
verses.16:10: And the king said, "What is there between me and you, sons of Zeruiah? Leave him alone so that he may curse, for the Lord commanded him to curse David; and who is there who would dare to say why he has done so?"
verses.16:11: And the king said to Abishai and to all his servants, "Look, my son, who came forth from my body, is seeking my life; how much more now a son of Jemini? Leave him alone so that he may curse according to the command of the Lord,
verses.16:12: if perhaps the Lord may look upon my affliction, and the Lord may return good to me for this cursing today."
verses.16:13: Therefore David and his companions were walking along the road with him. Meanwhile Shimei was walking along the ridge of the mountain on the side opposite him, cursing, throwing stones at him, and scattering dirt.
verses.16:14: So the king and all the people with him arrived weary, and they were refreshed there.
verses.16:15: Now Absalom and all his people entered Jerusalem, and Ahithophel also was with him.
verses.16:16: Now when Hushai the Archite, the friend of David, came to Absalom, he spoke to him: "Hail, king! Hail, king!"
verses.16:17: Absalom said to him, "Is this your kindness to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"
verses.16:18: And Hushai answered Absalom, "Not at all, for I will belong to the one whom the Lord, and all this people, and all Israel have chosen, and with him I will remain.
verses.16:19: And to add this as well, whom am I going to serve? Is it not the king's son? Just as I obeyed your father, so I will obey you also."
verses.16:20: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Take counsel on what we ought to do."
verses.16:21: And Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left behind to guard the house, so that when all Israel hears that you have defiled your father, their hands may be strengthened with you."
verses.16:22: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the rooftop, and he went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
verses.16:23: Now the counsel of Ahithophel that he gave in those days was as if someone consulted God; such was all the counsel of Ahithophel, both when he was with David and when he was with Absalom.
verses.17:1: Then Ahithophel said to Absalom, "I will choose for myself twelve thousand men, and rising up, I will pursue David tonight.
verses.17:2: And rushing upon him (since he is weary and his hands are weak), I will strike him; and when all the people who are with him have fled, I will strike the abandoned king.
verses.17:3: And I will bring back all the people, just as one man usually returns; for it is one man whom you are seeking, and all the people will be at peace."
verses.17:4: And his speech pleased Absalom and all the elders of Israel.
verses.17:5: Then Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Archite, and let us hear what he himself also says."
verses.17:6: And when Hushai had come to Absalom, Absalom said to him, "Ahithophel has spoken this kind of speech; ought we to do it or not? What counsel do you give?"
verses.17:7: And Hushai said to Absalom, "The counsel that Ahithophel has given this time is not good."
verses.17:8: And again Hushai added, "You know that your father and the men who are with him are very mighty and bitter in spirit, just as if a she-bear robbed of her cubs were raging in the forest; moreover, your father is a warrior, and he will not stay with the people.
verses.17:9: Perhaps he is now hiding in pits, or in some place, whichever he chooses; and when anyone at all falls at the beginning, whoever hears will hear of it and say, 'A slaughter has taken place among the people who were following Absalom.'
verses.17:10: And even the mightiest man, whose heart is like that of a lion, will melt with terror; for all the people of Israel know that your father is mighty, and that all who are with him are strong.
verses.17:11: Rather, this seems to me to be right counsel. Let all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan as far as Beersheba, countless like the sand of the sea, and you will be in their midst.
verses.17:12: And we will rush upon him in whatever place he may be found, and we will cover him just as dew usually falls upon the ground; and of the men who are with him, we will not leave even a single one.
verses.17:13: And if he has entered any city, all Israel will place ropes around that city, and we will drag it into the stream, so that not even a pebble of it will be found."
verses.17:14: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." Yet by the Lord's will the useful counsel of Ahithophel was thwarted, so that the Lord might bring calamity upon Absalom.
verses.17:15: And Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "In such and such a way Ahithophel gave counsel to Absalom and the elders of Israel, and I gave such and such counsel.
verses.17:16: Now therefore, send quickly and report to David, saying, 'Do not stay tonight in the plains of the wilderness, but cross over without delay, so that the king and all the people who are with him may not be swallowed up.'"
verses.17:17: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were standing beside the spring of Rogel; a maidservant went and reported to them. And they set out to carry the message to King David, for they could not be seen or enter the city.
verses.17:18: However, a certain young man saw them and told Absalom; but they went with hurried step into the house of a certain man in Bahurim who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it.
verses.17:19: Then the woman took and spread a covering over the mouth of the well, as if drying crushed barley; and thus the matter remained hidden.
verses.17:20: And when the servants of Absalom came into the house, they said to the woman, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" And the woman answered them, "They passed on in haste, after tasting a little water." And those who were searching, when they did not find them, returned to Jerusalem.
verses.17:21: And when they had gone away, the others came up out of the well, and going on, they reported to King David and said, "Rise up and cross the river quickly, because Ahithophel has given counsel of this kind against you."
verses.17:22: So David rose up, and all the people who were with him, and they crossed the Jordan until daybreak; and not even a single one was left who had not crossed the river.
verses.17:23: Now Ahithophel, seeing that his counsel had not been carried out, saddled his donkey, and rose up and went away to his house and to his city; and having put his house in order, he died by hanging, and he was buried in the tomb of his father.
verses.17:24: Now David came into the camp, and Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
verses.17:25: And Absalom appointed Amasa in place of Joab over the army. Now Amasa was the son of a man who was called Ithra of Jezreel, who went in to Abigail, the daughter of Nahash, the sister of Zeruiah, who was the mother of Joab.
verses.17:26: And Israel encamped with Absalom in the land of Gilead.
verses.17:27: And when David had come into the camp, Shobi the son of Nahash, from Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite, from Rogelim,
verses.17:28: brought to him bedding, rugs, and earthenware vessels; wheat, barley, flour, parched grain, beans, lentils, and roasted chickpeas,
verses.17:29: and honey, butter, sheep, and fatted calves; and they gave them to David and to the people who were with him to eat, for they supposed that the people were exhausted by hunger and thirst in the wilderness.
verses.18:1: Therefore, having reviewed his people, David appointed tribunes and centurions over them,
verses.18:2: and he placed a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, the brother of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Ittai, who was from Gath. And the king said to the people, "I also will go out with you."
verses.18:3: And the people answered, "You will not go out; for if we flee, it will not greatly matter to them about us, or if half of us fall, they will not care much, because you alone are counted for ten thousand. Therefore it is better that you be a protection for us in the city."
verses.18:4: To them the king said, "What seems right to you, this I will do." So the king stood beside the gate, and the people were going out in their companies, by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.18:5: And the king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, "Preserve the boy Absalom for me." And all the people heard the king commanding all the leaders on behalf of Absalom.
verses.18:6: So the people went out into the field against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.
